dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Okay, so I'm looking at two flats. I need your honest opinion.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Tell me everything. Which one is closer to the university?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Flat A is much closer — about eight minutes on foot. Flat B is at least twenty-five minutes by bus.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's already a big difference. What about price?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Flat B is cheaper. About 15% less than Flat A per month. But Flat A includes utilities.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Hmm. With utilities included, Flat A might actually be the better deal.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: That's what I was thinking too. And Flat A is significantly larger — two full rooms versus one.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Is it as bright as Flat B? Light is really important.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Flat A is darker, unfortunately. Lower floor, faces north. Flat B has much better natural light.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's a real downside. I struggle more in darker rooms.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Me too. But Flat B is noisier — it's right on the main road.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Which is the quieter neighbourhood overall?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Flat A — by far. It's a residential street. Much more peaceful.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: And is the building itself in better condition?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Flat A is newer and better maintained. The landlord seems more reliable too.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Zhibek, it sounds like Flat A is the obvious choice — except for the light.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I know. I just keep thinking — is bright light worth 25 extra minutes of commuting every day?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Probably not. Time is harder to get back than sunlight.

questions.text: "Flat A is much ___ than Flat B." Which comparative is correct?
questions.hint: "close" is a one-syllable adjective → add -er: closer. "Much closer than..." ✅

questions.text: "Flat B has ___ better natural light." Which intensifier fits?
questions.hint: "much" intensifies comparatives: "much better", "much closer", "much more expensive". Stronger than "a bit".

questions.text: "Is it ___ as Flat B?" — comparing equal quality.
questions.hint: "as + adjective + as" = equal comparison. "Is it AS BRIGHT AS Flat B?" ✅

questions.text: "Flat A is the ___ neighbourhood overall." Use superlative.
questions.hint: Superlative of "quiet": quietest (short adjective + -est). "the quietest neighbourhood." ✅

questions.text: "Flat B is more noisier than Flat A" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "Flat B is noisier than Flat A." — "noisy" ends in -y → drop y + ier. NEVER "more noisier"!

questions.text: "Flat A is ___ better deal." Choose the article.
questions.hint: "the better deal" — we use "the" before comparatives when comparing TWO specific things. "the better of the two".

questions.text: "Flat A is ___ maintained than Flat B." Use comparative.
"Flat A is by far the ___ choice." Use superlative.
questions.hint: "obvious" is a long adjective (3 syllables) → superlative: "the most obvious". ✅
